questions.prompt: Complete the polite request: "Would you mind ___ the window, please?"
questions.explanation: After "Would you mind", the verb takes -ing: Would you mind opening the window? "to open" is the classic mistake — many languages use an infinitive there, English does not; "open" and "opened" are not the -ing form.
When you offer help, YOU are the helper, so the question starts with "Can I": Can I help you? The three other sentences ask the other person to help you — they are requests, not offers.

questions.prompt: Complete the suggestion: "What about ___ to the fun fair on Tuesday?"
questions.explanation: "What about" ends with the word "about", and after it a verb takes -ing: What about going to the fun fair? The bare verb "go" belongs after Let's, Shall we or Why don't we; "we go" needs the opener "I suggest that".

questions.prompt: Karim is completely sure that Jack forgot the time. Which sentence expresses his certainty?

options.text: I hope that Jack has not forgotten the time.
There's no doubt Jack forgot the time.

questions.explanation: "There's no doubt" + a full sentence expresses certainty: There's no doubt Jack forgot the time. "Perhaps" and "Maybe" show that the speaker is NOT sure, and "I hope that" expresses a wish, not a certainty.

The person who feels the interest is "interested": I'm interested in photography. "interesting" describes the thing that gives interest (It sounds interesting), so "I'm interesting in" is the classic swap; "interest" and "interests" are not adjectives here.
